q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of self-adhesive labels?
title: Self-adhesive label footprint per m2
short: Multiply the label stock used, including matrix waste and liner, by your supplier's per-square-metre or per-kg figure. Add printing ink, press electricity and UV curing, die cutting and rewinding, then divide plant energy by square metres of labels passed.

ul: Face stock: paper, PP or PE film.
Adhesive and silicone release liner, which is often thrown away by the user.
Flexo or digital press with UV or hot air dryers.

p: Report per square metre of printed labels; buyers can convert to per label from the label size.

example.title: Worked example: label plant per square metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 24,850 / 700,000 = 0.0355 kg CO2 per square metre
Add label stock, liner and ink for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
